items.title: Increasingly this will be the new job description for a lot of roles, not just coding
items.text: Increasingly this will be the new job description for a lot of roles, not just coding. We’re clearly moving from a world where agents help us do our work incrementally better or faster, to us helping agents do their work. This turns everyone in one of these positions to that of a manager of a team of agents, instead of an individual contributor with just some added leverage from AI. The biggest areas of impact will be information-heavy jobs, like coding, cybersecurity, legal work, biotech, engineering, and many other fields. And as a result, in these jobs your leverage will begin to be decoupled from the normal ratio of hours spent working to output generated. For essentially the history of...

items.title: Own your intelligence
items.text: Own your intelligence. Anyone that opposes this has something to sell you (perhaps your own intelligence back to you.) Local models need to continue proliferating. The “absolute unit” massive models may be out of reach for now locally, so your best option is to, indeed, keep your options open. Own your harness, data, connections, runtime: your agents. Embrace open source.

items.title: "It really makes you question, why do you want a person in your product
items.text: "It really makes you question, why do you want a person in your product? Is your product something that needs a UI?" From @jacalulu (product director at @GoogleLabs): "Anything that involves me creating something. Anything where I want to learn something, there might be a reason for me to interact. Anytime I want to be entertained or consume something, I'm still the one using the product. But there are definitely products that I use today that I would be more than happy to not use, or at least not be the main person interacting with the interface." 📌 Watch our full episode here: https://t.co/8hLt6x6atQ
